我是个很敏感又很迟钝的人，很奇怪，我自己也搞不明白为什么两种看似相反的特质会同时存在在我身上。

我常常忘记别人觉得根本不可能忘记的事情，比如吃完饭很自然就走了没付钱。然后在某一天早上醒来时突然惊觉“糟了，那次忘付钱了！”再比如，小时候我只要坚定地告诉自己，“国庆节只放三天假”，再让周围的人都配合骗我，就可以洗脑成功，从而获得“假期延长”的意外之喜。我也很难听出别人话里的弦外之音，那些暗戳戳的指责，嘲讽，嫉妒，赞赏……我当时都一概没感觉，但那些东西会在某一刻突然午夜梦回，变成迟到的顿悟“原来那时候是这个意思！”

但我知道我并不是不知道，只是这些信号不知为何没有传到大脑的逻辑系统里，我的潜意识是捕捉到并且在分析的。因此我非常非常信赖我的直觉，我知道我的直觉比我的逻辑强大。于是乎，那些被称作“宿命”的事情常常发生在我身上。当我的逻辑终于跟上直觉时，我已经跟随直觉做出那个选择很久了，而那个选择带来的影响会逐渐让我的逻辑明白当时直觉的深意。

因此，我一直痴迷于用逻辑去观察和分析我的直觉，它太强大太迷人了。“它究竟捕捉到了什么？”“为何当时会有要这样做的感觉呢？”我知道冥冥之中它在保护我免受重大伤害，又在悄悄引导我走向人生一个又一个我需要完成的课题，让我和未来更好的自己相遇。

我的直觉，我知道你可以听到，在这里我想和你说声“谢谢”。

entry.content:
Promises is a collaborative album between British electronic producer Floating Points (Sam Shepherd), the legendary saxophonist Pharoah Sanders, and the London Symphony Orchestra. The result is something that defies easy categorization.

The Structure

The album is built around a single seven-note motif that repeats, shifts, and evolves across nine movements. What begins as a minimalist harpsichord figure gradually opens up into sweeping orchestral passages and Sanders’ unmistakable tenor saxophone — warm, searching, spiritual.

It’s less an album and more a single continuous piece. The 46-minute runtime feels both epic and intimate, demanding your full attention yet never abrasive.

Why It Stays With Me

There’s something deeply meditative about Promises. Every time I listen, I notice a new detail — a subtle synth layer, a shift in the string arrangement, a breath between saxophone phrases. It rewards patience in an age that rarely asks for it.

It was also one of Pharoah Sanders’ final recordings before his passing in 2022, which gives every note an added poignancy.

Put on headphones, close your eyes, and let it wash over you.
entry.summary: Floating through space with Floating Points and Pharoah Sanders — a 46-minute journey that transcends genre.
entry.title: Promises

entry.content:
Playing Tunic feels like being a kid again, discovering a Japanese import game without knowing the language. It’s a game built around the joy of not knowing — and the thrill of figuring things out.

The Manual Is the Game

The central mechanic is brilliant: you collect pages of an in-game instruction manual written in a fictional language. Each page reveals game mechanics you might have been able to do all along — you just didn’t know it yet. It turns game literacy into a puzzle itself.

The manual is also a map, a hint system, a lore book, and occasionally, the solution to puzzles hidden in plain sight. The way it layers knowledge is unlike anything else in the medium.

Combat & World Design

The combat feels like a tighter, more deliberate take on the Zelda/Souls formula — simple on the surface but with surprising depth. The isometric world is dense with secrets, many hidden behind perspective tricks or cryptic environmental clues.

Who Should Play

  • Fans of Zelda, Dark Souls, and Fez
  • Anyone who misses physical game manuals
  • Players who love discovering secrets without waypoints or quest markers

The less you know going in, the better.
entry.summary: A love letter to classic instruction manuals wrapped in an isometric adventure that trusts you to figure things out.

entry.content:
大部分人有筛选朋友圈子的意识，但2026年了，很多人每天和信息流打交道时间已经比和真人多了，却比较少有人提过需要同样筛选自己的网络圈子。

我一般会定期整理自己的关注列表，如果我发现这个博主发的东西大部分是消耗我(这里消耗指只能引发情绪而不能激发思考的内容)或者我完全不感兴趣不想了解的，我会及时取消关注。我在关注每一个博主时也会审慎评估是否需要关注。

同时我会有意识增加自己主动搜索查看帖子的频率，减少被动接受算法推荐。我认为很多时候甚至有必要主动搜索与你认知完全相反的观点，去看为何这个观点存在支持者，他们的视角是怎样的，能够帮助养成批判性思考的能力。

还有我也会认真对待自己的收藏。收藏视频但让视频在收藏夹吃灰是很不负责的行为，和买了书不读一个道理，享受了占有的快感但对自己一点用没有。对于知识类视频及时消化内容把他们从收藏夹释放才是正解。

最后的最后很重要的一点，也关注点让自己放松的不用动脑子的内容。刷这些软件毕竟还是图一乐，也别整太严肃了。在放松和获取知识间达到微妙平衡才是正解~

我有个朋友是当代女性主义者，之前很多时候我有点难以接受她的观点，也不是不认同，就是感觉没必要反应这么激烈。包括大家都说好的那些女性电影《还有明天》以及《我，许可》，我都没办法完全共鸣。会更喜欢《好东西》，《给阿嬷的情书》这种更加温和更加细腻的女性主义电影。

后来我明白了，是我身处的环境在这方面太健康了，环境的局限导致我没有真正感受过女性困境。因此会下意识觉得女性困境更多出于女性个体的自主选择，低估了环境对女性的压迫。大家觉得进步的事情在我眼里都是正常现象。就比如《还有明天》中女主无论私奔还是去投选票我都觉得“OK我尊重你的选择”，并不会觉得惊喜。反而她去投选票我会担心她回家会不会继续被丈夫家暴。**我的温和本身没有错，但如果想要在权利结构本就失衡的局面下夺回权利，只有温和是不够的，女性需要一批激进的斗士去发声去争取。**我也许没办法成为这样的人，但我应该更加理解和尊重为之努力的人，为她们大声加油才是。

不过我的根本观点还是不解决阶级矛盾是不可能真正解决两性矛盾的。但任何微小的改变都是我期待看见的，毕竟我也是受益者，不是嘛:)

entry.content:
Charlotte Wells’ debut feature is a masterclass in restraint. Set mostly during a father-daughter holiday at a Turkish resort in the late 1990s, the film unfolds as a series of fragmented memories.

The Power of What’s Unsaid

Paul Mescal delivers a career-defining performance as Calum, a young father hiding profound sadness behind a gentle smile. But the film truly belongs to Frankie Corio as Sophie, whose 11-year-old gaze captures everything and nothing at once.

What makes Aftersun so devastating is how it trusts its audience. Wells never explains Calum’s pain — we only see it through Sophie’s incomplete understanding, replayed decades later through adult eyes searching for clues she missed.

Standout Moments

  • The “Under Pressure” sequence — one of the most emotionally overwhelming scenes I’ve ever experienced
  • The recurring motif of the strobe-lit dance floor, Sophie reaching for a father she can never quite reach
  • The final pan, which I won’t spoil, but it broke me completely

A film that doesn’t just reward rewatches — it deepens with them.
entry.summary: A quietly devastating portrait of memory, fatherhood, and the things we can't understand until it's too late.
entry.title: Aftersun

entry.content:
我的电影top10之一，每过几年必定翻出来重温的电影。对这部电影哪个部分最有共鸣会反映人生当下最关注的议题是什么。

小时候读了太多不适合那个年纪的书，总是思考和自己阅历不匹配的哲学问题，整天无意义的忧郁。现在终于明白，那些问题的出路在于和他者的碰撞，一段关系越深刻，越能从别人这面镜子里窥见真正的自己。毕竟每个人都没有办法看到自己的后脑勺不是嘛？洋洋真的是大哲学家。

都说性格决定命运，了解了精神分析理论后，我觉得倒不如说是潜意识的形态决定命运，那些由每个人天生特质加上经历塑造的独一无二的潜意识，让我们作出一个个必然的人生选择。就像NJ在30年后遇见初恋情人，心动归心动，却发现如果重来一次，“还是会重复过去的选择，再来一次感觉也没什么必要”。从这点上来说，命运的确无法改变。但如果能够看到潜意识的创伤，理解自己为何会这样，当看见的那一刻，潜意识就已经发生了重构，再加上有意识的修正练习，命运也会随之改变。 这也是我对“命运”这个词现在的理解，“命”是既定的，但“运”可以干预。

跑个题，突然想到一个GalGame《命运石之门》。主角凤凰院凶真能够在不同世界线上跳跃保持记忆，却发现每条世界线都有遗憾。每个人在这个世界上都有自己的困境。我现在觉得真正的幸福是不可能的，但可以像微积分一样无限逼近，到达“命运石之门”这条完美世界线。方法其实和游戏里有点像：先去探索不同的世界线，即探索自己的潜意识会引导自己做出什么选择(不同人的课题不一样要自己去发现)。比如我就特别圣母特别有拯救欲，我特别喜欢那些看起来有“破碎”特质的人。因此我玩星露谷会喜欢谢恩，在现实中也会对这种人心动，会想要通过“拯救”他们确认自己的价值和独特性。但其实是不健康的，他人的课题是我不需要也不能干涉的。意识到的那一刻，其实就已经具备了控制这种冲动的力量。当别人向你寻求帮助，大可以发挥自己的圣母心让它变成乐于助人的品格。但当别人没有发出信号，自己的心还在拼命呼唤“他需要帮助，我要拯救他”时，像凤凰院凶真一样欺骗一下自己，稳住自己的那颗企图越界的心。这一刻，命运的世界线便已悄然改变。

A film that doesn’t just reward rewatches — it deepens with them.

entry.content:
Between life and death there is a library, and within that library, the shelves go on forever. Every book provides a chance to try another life you could have lived.

Why I Loved It

Matt Haig manages to wrap profound philosophical questions in a warm, accessible story. The idea of the Midnight Library — a place where you can sample all the lives you might have lived — is both comforting and haunting.

The writing is simple but effective, and Nora Seed is a protagonist many of us can relate to: someone who feels like they’ve disappointed everyone, including themselves.

Key Takeaways

  • Regret is a trap. Every choice closes some doors and opens others.
  • The “perfect” life doesn’t exist — every path has its own struggles.
  • What matters is being present in the life you’re actually living.

“The only way to learn is to live.”
entry.summary: A beautifully woven tale about second chances and the infinite possibilities of life.
entry.title: The Midnight Library
